subject: Money
title: Goldsmith Bankers
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Goldsmith Bankers.

hook.text: London goldsmiths in the 1600s had strong vaults. People paid them to store gold. Receipts became money.

buildup.text: Depositors traded receipts instead of withdrawing gold. Lighter, easier, safer. Paper money was born.

discovery.text: Goldsmiths noticed most gold sat untouched. They started lending it out and keeping only a fraction on hand.

twist.text: This was the birth of fractional reserve banking. One vault of gold backed many times its value in receipts.

climax.text: Modern banking's core trick—lending money you hold for others—began with goldsmiths who got creative.

punchline.text: Your bank does the same thing. Right now.

quiz.question: What key banking practice did goldsmiths invent?
